claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-211010.summary: Keep the machine on a RHEL 9 release that Red Hat still supports with security patches; an end-of-life release cannot be fixed when new vulnerabilities appear.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-211010.caution: Upgrading to a supported release is a major change that should be scheduled and tested against the applications on the box.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-211045.summary: Stop systemd from rebooting the machine when someone at the console presses Ctrl-Alt-Delete seven times in two seconds, by setting CtrlAltDelBurstAction=none in a systemd drop-in file, so an accidental key press cannot take the system down.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-211050.summary: Disable and mask the ctrl-alt-del.target so pressing Ctrl-Alt-Delete at the console no longer reboots the machine and an accidental key press cannot cause an outage.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212020.summary: Give the GRUB boot loader superuser a non-obvious account name (not root, admin, or administrator) so an attacker at the console has to guess both the name and the password to get into single-user or maintenance mode.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212020.caution: A mistake in /etc/grub.d/01_users or when regenerating grub.cfg can leave the system unable to boot or lock you out of boot-time recovery; keep the new superuser name and password recorded somewhere safe.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-214015.summary: Make the package manager verify the GPG signature of every package it downloads from a repository (gpgcheck=1 in /etc/dnf/dnf.conf) so tampered or unofficial packages cannot be installed unnoticed.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-214015.caution: Packages from repositories without a trusted signing key will fail to install until the key is imported.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-214020.summary: Make the package manager verify the GPG signature of packages installed from local files too (localpkg_gpgcheck=1 in /etc/dnf/dnf.conf) so a hand-copied package file cannot bypass signature checking.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-214020.caution: Locally built or unsigned RPMs will be refused until they are signed with a key the system trusts.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-214025.summary: Every repository file in /etc/yum.repos.d/ must have gpgcheck set to 1 so packages from any configured source are signature-checked before installation.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-214025.caution: Third-party repositories that do not provide signing keys will stop working until a key is imported or the repository is removed.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215015.summary: Remove the vsftpd package; FTP sends passwords and file contents in clear text, so an encrypted alternative such as SSH must be used instead.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215015.caution: Confirm nothing still depends on FTP file transfers before removing the server.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215060.summary: Remove the tftp-server package unless TFTP is genuinely needed; if it is, run the daemon with the -s option so it can only serve files from /var/lib/tftpboot and not the rest of the file system.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215060.caution: If TFTP is used for things like router configuration transfers, removing it or changing its serving directory will break those workflows; document the approved use first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215100.summary: Install the crypto-policies package so the system can apply one central set of approved ciphers across the operating system and its applications.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215105.summary: Set the systemwide cryptographic policy to FIPS (with a STIG subpolicy that limits SSH ciphers and MACs) so all services use FIPS 140-3-approved hashes and RSA keys of at least 2048 bits.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215105.caution: The change needs a reboot and can break connections to older systems or applications that rely on SHA1, small RSA keys, or ciphers the FIPS policy disallows.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231190.summary: Local disk partitions holding data that needs at-rest protection must be encrypted (for example with LUKS) so a stolen or discarded disk cannot be read; this is Not Applicable if encryption is documented as provided elsewhere, such as by a hypervisor or storage array.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231190.caution: Encrypting partitions on an already installed system means resizing and rebuilding partitions, which risks data loss; plan it at install time or take a full backup first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252070.summary: There must be no shosts.equiv files anywhere on the system, because they enable SSH host-based authentication that lets connections in without a real user login or two-factor check.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252070.caution: Any host that relied on host-based trust to reach this machine will need proper user credentials instead.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252075.summary: There must be no .shosts files in any home directory or elsewhere, because they allow individual users to set up SSH host-based trust that bypasses normal login and two-factor authentication.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252075.caution: Users who relied on .shosts trust for scripted logins will need to switch to keys or another approved method.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255040.summary: Set PermitEmptyPasswords no in the SSH server configuration so nobody can log in remotely to an account whose password is blank.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255040.caution: Restarting sshd applies the change; existing sessions are unaffected, but any account that genuinely has no password will no longer be reachable over SSH.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255050.summary: Set UsePAM yes in the SSH server configuration so SSH logins go through the PAM account and session checks, which is what enforces things like time-of-day restrictions and proper login environment handling.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255050.caution: Restarting sshd is required; check that the PAM configuration itself is sane first, since SSH logins will now depend on it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255064.summary: The SSH client must only offer the four FIPS 140-3 approved AES ciphers listed in the crypto-policies openssh.config; this is achieved by reinstalling crypto-policies and setting the systemwide policy to FIPS.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255064.caution: Outbound SSH from this machine to older servers that only support other ciphers will stop working, and a restart is recommended for the policy to take full effect.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255065.summary: The SSH server must only accept the four FIPS 140-3 approved AES ciphers listed in the crypto-policies opensshserver.config; this is achieved by reinstalling crypto-policies and setting the systemwide policy to FIPS.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255065.caution: Older SSH clients or automation that cannot negotiate these ciphers will be locked out; test from your normal management hosts before restarting.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255070.summary: The SSH client must only offer the four hmac-sha2 message authentication codes listed in the crypto-policies openssh.config; this is achieved by reinstalling crypto-policies and setting the systemwide policy to FIPS.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255070.caution: Connections to remote servers that only support weaker MACs will fail, and a restart is recommended for the policy to take full effect.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255075.summary: The SSH server must only accept the four hmac-sha2 message authentication codes listed in the crypto-policies opensshserver.config; this is achieved by reinstalling crypto-policies and setting the systemwide policy to FIPS.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255075.caution: Legacy SSH clients that cannot use these MACs will be unable to connect; verify your management tooling before applying.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271040.summary: If the GNOME desktop is installed, set AutomaticLoginEnable=false in /etc/gdm/custom.conf so the machine never logs a user in at the graphical screen without a password; Not Applicable on systems with no graphical interface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271040.caution: Kiosk-style setups that depend on automatic login will start prompting for credentials.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411100.summary: Only the root account may have UID 0; any other account with UID 0 must be given a different UID, because every extra UID-0 account is another password an attacker can try for full control. Administrators should get root access through a properly configured privilege-escalation tool instead.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411100.caution: Changing an account's UID can break ownership of its files and any service running under it; identify why the account exists before renumbering it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-431010.summary: SELinux must be running in Enforcing mode now and be set to SELINUX=enforcing in /etc/selinux/config so it comes up that way after every reboot, confining system services to what their policy allows.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-431010.caution: Switching from disabled or permissive to enforcing can block applications with incorrect labels or missing policy; review audit denials in permissive mode first and note a reboot is required.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611025.summary: Remove the nullok option from the PAM system-auth and password-auth files (or enable the without-nullok authselect feature) so no account can log in with an empty password.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611025.caution: Any account that currently has an empty password will be unable to log in until it is given one; use authselect if it manages PAM, since hand edits may be overwritten.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-671010.summary: The kernel must be running in FIPS mode (/proc/sys/crypto/fips_enabled reports 1). On an already installed system this cannot be fixed in place; the STIG treats it as a permanent finding until the system is reinstalled with fips=1.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-671010.caution: Meeting this rule means a full reinstall, and FIPS mode disallows weaker algorithms that some applications may still depend on.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-671020.summary: If the Libreswan ipsec service is installed, /etc/ipsec.conf must include the crypto-policies libreswan.config so IP tunnels follow the systemwide FIPS algorithm policy instead of their own; Not Applicable if ipsec is not installed.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-671020.caution: Existing tunnels negotiated with algorithms outside the system policy may fail to reconnect after the change.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-672020.summary: The active crypto policy must match what the crypto-policies package generated, with no locally edited back-end files; if update-crypto-policies --check reports a mismatch, reinstall crypto-policies and set the policy to FIPS.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-672020.caution: Reinstalling wipes any hand-made overrides in the back-end files, so services that depended on those tweaks may change behavior after the recommended restart.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-672050.summary: If the bind package is installed, the options section of /etc/named.conf must include the crypto-policies bind.config so the DNS server follows the systemwide crypto policy; Not Applicable if bind is not installed.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-672050.caution: DNSSEC or TSIG setups using algorithms the system policy disallows will stop working once the include is added.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-171011.summary: On systems with the GNOME desktop, the graphical login screen must show the exact Standard Mandatory DOD Notice and Consent Banner text, configured through the dconf login-screen banner-message-text setting; Not Applicable without a graphical interface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-171011.caution: The banner text must match the STIG wording exactly, including line breaks, or the check still fails.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-211015.summary: Keep security patches and updates installed at the frequency your organization's patching policy requires, using dnf update from the configured repositories; the check reviews dnf history against that policy and any IAVA notices.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-211015.caution: Applying all updates at once can change kernel and library versions, so test and schedule the update window rather than running it blindly on production.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-211020.summary: Replace the default text in /etc/issue with the exact Standard Mandatory DOD Notice and Consent Banner so anyone logging in at a command-line console sees the required legal notice before they get access.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-211020.caution: The banner wording must match the STIG text exactly or the check still fails.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-211030.summary: The system should boot to the command line (multi-user.target) rather than a graphical login unless the ISSO has documented a need for a graphical interface, because display managers add attack surface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-211030.caution: Changing the default target means the graphical desktop will no longer appear at boot, which surprises users of workstation-style systems.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-211040.summary: The systemd-journald service must be running so the system keeps the log information needed to diagnose failures and recover.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-211055.summary: Disable and mask debug-shell.service, which would otherwise give anyone with physical console access a root shell with no password.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212010.summary: On BIOS-booted systems, set a GRUB2 superuser password (stored encrypted in /boot/grub2/user.cfg) so nobody can edit boot options or drop into recovery from the boot menu without it; Not Applicable on UEFI systems.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212010.caution: Record the boot loader password somewhere safe; without it you cannot alter kernel arguments or use single-user recovery at the console.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212015.summary: Remove the systemd.confirm_spawn kernel argument from all boot entries so a console user cannot step through boot interactively and skip services such as auditing or the firewall.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212025.summary: The /boot/grub2/grub.cfg file must be group-owned by root so no less-privileged group can read or alter the boot configuration.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212030.summary: The /boot/grub2/grub.cfg file must be owned by root because it holds sensitive boot configuration that only root should control.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212035.summary: Add vsyscall=none to the kernel arguments of every boot entry and to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX in /etc/default/grub to disable the legacy virtual system call page, unless the ISSO has documented a need for it.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212035.caution: Very old binaries that still rely on vsyscall will crash after the next reboot, so confirm no legacy applications need it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212040.summary: Add page_poison=1 to the kernel arguments of every boot entry and to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX so freed memory pages are overwritten, which detects and blocks many use-after-free exploits.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212040.caution: Takes effect only after a reboot and adds a small amount of memory-management overhead.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212045.summary: Add init_on_free=1 to the kernel command line in GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX, regenerate the GRUB configuration, and reboot, so memory is cleared when freed and use-after-free bugs are harder to exploit.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212045.caution: Requires a reboot and adds some overhead on memory-intensive workloads.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213010.summary: Set the kernel.dmesg_restrict sysctl to 1 in a /etc/sysctl.d/ drop-in so only privileged users can read the kernel message buffer, which can leak addresses and hardware details useful to an attacker.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213010.caution: Unprivileged users and monitoring scripts that read dmesg will lose access.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213015.summary: Set the kernel.perf_event_paranoid sysctl to 2 in a /etc/sysctl.d/ drop-in so ordinary users cannot use kernel performance profiling to observe system internals.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213015.caution: Developers running perf as a normal user will need elevated privileges to profile.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213020.summary: Set the kernel.kexec_load_disabled sysctl to 1 in a /etc/sysctl.d/ drop-in so a running system cannot load and switch to a different kernel image, which would bypass boot-time verification.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213020.caution: This setting cannot be undone without a reboot, and it conflicts with kexec-based fast reboots or crash-dump kernels that need to load after boot.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213025.summary: Set the kernel.kptr_restrict sysctl to 1 in a /etc/sysctl.d/ drop-in so kernel memory addresses are hidden from unprivileged users, making it harder to build exploits.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213030.summary: Set the fs.protected_hardlinks sysctl to 1 in a /etc/sysctl.d/ drop-in so users can only create hard links to files they own or can write to, closing a common privilege-escalation trick.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213035.summary: Set the fs.protected_symlinks sysctl to 1 in a /etc/sysctl.d/ drop-in so symlinks in world-writable directories are only followed when it is safe to do so, blocking a common symlink-race privilege escalation.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213040.summary: Set kernel.core_pattern to |/bin/false in a /etc/sysctl.d/ drop-in so crashing programs never write core dumps to disk, since a dump can contain passwords and other sensitive memory contents; documented ISSO exceptions are allowed.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213040.caution: Developers or vendors who rely on core dumps to debug crashes will no longer get them; agree an exception with the ISSO if that is a real need.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213045.summary: Prevent the atm kernel module from loading by adding install and blacklist lines to /etc/modprobe.d/atm.conf, so flaws in the rarely used Asynchronous Transfer Mode code cannot be exploited; a documented ISSO requirement is an acceptable exception.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213050.summary: Prevent the can kernel module from loading by adding install and blacklist lines to /etc/modprobe.d/can.conf, so flaws in the Controller Area Network code cannot be exploited; a documented ISSO requirement is an acceptable exception.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213050.caution: Systems that talk to CAN-bus hardware will lose that capability.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213055.summary: Prevent the firewire-core kernel module from loading by adding install and blacklist lines to /etc/modprobe.d/firewire-core.conf, closing off FireWire and its known direct-memory-access risks; a documented ISSO requirement is an acceptable exception.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213055.caution: Any FireWire-attached devices will stop working.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213060.summary: Prevent the sctp kernel module from loading by adding install and blacklist lines to /etc/modprobe.d/sctp.conf so the seldom-used SCTP network protocol cannot be an attack path; a documented ISSO requirement is an acceptable exception.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213060.caution: Telecom and some clustering software use SCTP; confirm nothing on the system needs it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213065.summary: Prevent the tipc kernel module from loading by adding install and blacklist lines to /etc/modprobe.d/tipc.conf so the Transparent Inter Process Communication protocol cannot be an attack path; a documented ISSO requirement is an acceptable exception.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213070.summary: Set kernel.randomize_va_space to 2 in /etc/sysctl.d/99-kernel_randomize_va_space.conf and remove any conflicting sysctl entries so full address space layout randomization is on, making memory-corruption exploits much harder.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213070.caution: Any other sysctl file that sets this parameter to a different value causes a finding, so search all the listed locations for conflicts.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213075.summary: Set kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled to 1 in a /etc/sysctl.d/ drop-in so only privileged processes can use the bpf system call, removing a known route for kernel privilege escalation.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213075.caution: Once set, this cannot be reverted without a reboot, and unprivileged tools that load BPF programs will fail.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213080.summary: Set kernel.yama.ptrace_scope to 1 in a /etc/sysctl.d/ drop-in so a process can only debug or inspect its own child processes, stopping one user process from reading another's memory.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213080.caution: Debuggers and tools that attach to already-running processes will need root or explicit permission.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213085.summary: Set ProcessSizeMax=0 in /etc/systemd/coredump.conf so systemd does not capture core dump backtraces that could expose sensitive memory; Not Applicable if core dumps are already disabled under RHEL-09-213040, and documented ISSO exceptions are allowed.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213085.caution: Crash troubleshooting through systemd-coredump will no longer produce usable data.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213090.summary: Set Storage=none in /etc/systemd/coredump.conf so systemd does not save core dumps to disk; Not Applicable if core dumps are already disabled under RHEL-09-213040, and documented ISSO exceptions are allowed.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213090.caution: Crash troubleshooting that depends on saved core files will no longer work.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213095.summary: Add a global hard core 0 limit at the top of /etc/security/limits.conf (or one file in limits.d) and remove any per-user or per-group entries allowing larger dumps, so no user process can write a core file; Not Applicable if RHEL-09-213040 already disables dumps.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213095.caution: Any user or group entry with a nonzero core limit is a finding, so review existing limits files rather than only adding the new line.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213100.summary: Mask systemd-coredump.socket so the system stops collecting and processing core dumps at all; Not Applicable if RHEL-09-213040 already disables dumps, and documented ISSO exceptions are allowed.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213100.caution: Crash analysis via coredumpctl will no longer be available.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213105.summary: Set user.max_user_namespaces to 0 in a /etc/sysctl.d/ drop-in so unprivileged users cannot create user namespaces, a feature that has repeatedly been used in kernel exploits; a documented ISSM requirement is an acceptable exception.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213105.caution: Rootless containers (for example Podman as a normal user), Flatpak, and some sandboxing tools depend on user namespaces and will break.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213110.summary: The CPU must report the nx flag (NX/XD enabled in BIOS or UEFI) and the kernel command line must not contain noexec, so the kernel can mark data memory as nonexecutable and block injected code from running.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213110.caution: Enabling NX/XD may require a firmware change and a reboot, which cannot be scripted from the operating system.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213115.summary: Disable and mask the kdump service so a kernel crash does not write a full memory image to disk, which could expose sensitive data and fill the file system.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-213115.caution: Without kdump you lose the crash dumps Red Hat support often asks for when diagnosing kernel panics.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-214010.summary: The Red Hat package-signing keys (release key 2 and auxiliary key 3) must be imported from /etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-redhat-release into the system keyring, and their fingerprints must match the values Red Hat publishes, so only genuine Red Hat packages are trusted.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-214010.caution: Comparing fingerprints against Red Hat's Product Signing Keys page is a manual step; importing a key from an untrusted source defeats the purpose.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-214030.summary: Every installed system file must still have the hash the RPM database expects (configuration files excluded); any file that has changed must be traced to its package and the package reinstalled, since altered binaries can indicate tampering.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-214030.caution: Before reinstalling, find out why a file changed; legitimate local modifications to non-config files will be overwritten.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215010.summary: Internet-connected systems must have the subscription-manager package installed so the machine can register with Red Hat and receive supported repositories and updates; Not Applicable on disconnected systems.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215020.summary: Remove the sendmail package; it was not designed with security in mind and cannot be properly confined by SELinux, so Postfix must be used for mail instead.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215020.caution: If the system actually sends mail through sendmail, set up Postfix first so local mail delivery does not silently stop.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215025.summary: Remove the nfs-utils package, which provides the kernel NFS server and tools such as showmount that expose information about NFS exports.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215025.caution: Removing nfs-utils also removes the ability to mount NFS shares, so confirm the system neither serves nor uses NFS.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215030.summary: Remove the ypserv package because NIS sends authentication data unencrypted, exposing passwords and session contents on the network.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215030.caution: If this host is still an NIS server for other machines, migrate those clients to another directory service first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215035.summary: No repository with epel in its name may be configured; remove the epel-release package and disable the epel repository so only packages from official, supported sources can be installed.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215035.caution: Packages already installed from EPEL stay on the system but will no longer receive updates, so identify and replace them.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215040.summary: Remove the telnet-server package; telnet is unencrypted and unnecessary when SSH is available.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215045.summary: Remove the gssproxy package unless NFS mounts are authorized and in use or the ISSO has documented a need for it; unused services only add attack surface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215045.caution: Kerberos-secured NFS depends on gssproxy, so check for authorized NFS use before removing it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215050.summary: Remove the iprutils package (IBM Power RAID adapter utilities) unless the ISSO has documented an operational need for it.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215050.caution: Systems with IBM Power RAID adapters may need this package to manage their storage.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215055.summary: Remove the tuned package unless the ISSO has documented an operational need for it, because unneeded services add attack surface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215055.caution: tuned applies performance profiles that some workloads (databases, virtualization hosts) rely on; removing it can change system performance.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215065.summary: Remove the quagga routing suite unless the ISSO has documented a need for the system to run OSPF, RIP, or BGP routing.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215065.caution: If the host really is acting as a router, removing quagga will drop its routing sessions.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215070.summary: The xorg-x11-server-common package must not be installed unless the ISSO has documented a need for a graphical interface; otherwise remove all xorg packages and set the default boot target to multi-user.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215070.caution: Removing xorg while working from within the graphical session kills that session immediately; switch to multi-user.target and run the removal from a text console.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215075.summary: Install the openssl-pkcs11 package so OpenSSL can use smart cards and other PKCS#11 tokens for multifactor authentication; Not Applicable if an approved alternate multifactor method is demonstrated.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215080.summary: Install the gnutls-utils package, which provides the GnuTLS command-line tools for working with TLS certificates and connections.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215085.summary: Install the nss-tools package, which provides the command-line tools for managing the NSS certificate and key databases used by many security-enabled applications.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215090.summary: Install the rng-tools package so the system can feed hardware random number generators into the entropy pool, which matters for generating strong keys and x509/PKI certificates.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215095.summary: Install the s-nail package, which supplies the mail command the system needs to email designated personnel about unauthorized configuration changes.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-215101.summary: Install the postfix package so the system has a mail transfer agent that can deliver audit failure notifications to the administrator or ISSO; Not Applicable if another system or service already handles those notifications.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231010.summary: User home directories (/home or its equivalent) must live on their own file system so restrictive mount options can be applied and users cannot fill up the partitions that hold logs and audit data.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231010.caution: Moving /home onto a new partition on a running system requires free disk space, copying all user data, and a maintenance window; get it wrong and users lose their files or cannot log in.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231015.summary: The /tmp directory must be its own file system so it can be mounted with restrictive options and programs writing temporary files cannot fill the root partition.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231015.caution: Repartitioning an installed system is disruptive; this is far easier to do at install time than to retrofit.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231035.summary: The /var/tmp directory must be its own file system so it can be mounted with restrictive options and temporary files cannot exhaust space on the root or /var partition.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231035.caution: Repartitioning an installed system is disruptive; this is far easier to do at install time than to retrofit.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231040.summary: If the autofs service is installed, it must be masked or disabled unless the ISSO has documented a need for automounting, because automatically mounted file systems can introduce untrusted content; Not Applicable if autofs is not installed.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231040.caution: Sites that automount NFS home directories or shared data through autofs will lose access to those paths.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231045.summary: The /home file system must be mounted with the nodev option in /etc/fstab so device files placed in a user's home directory are not interpreted, removing one way for a user to gain unauthorized privileges; if /home is not a separate file system this is automatically a finding.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231045.caution: Requires a separate /home file system; the option takes effect on remount or reboot.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231050.summary: The /home file system must be mounted with the nosuid option in /etc/fstab so setuid and setgid programs in home directories cannot run with elevated privileges; if /home is not a separate file system this is automatically a finding.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231050.caution: Requires a separate /home file system; the option takes effect on remount or reboot.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231055.summary: The /home file system must be mounted with the noexec option in /etc/fstab so binaries stored in user home directories cannot be executed directly; if /home is not a separate file system this is automatically a finding.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231055.caution: Users who build or run programs and scripts from their home directories will find they no longer execute, so plan an alternative location for legitimate work.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231065.summary: Every NFS mount listed in /etc/fstab must include the nodev option so device files on a remote export cannot be interpreted on this system; Not Applicable if no NFS mounts are configured.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231065.caution: Existing mounts must be remounted for the new option to apply.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231070.summary: Every NFS mount listed in /etc/fstab must carry the noexec option so that programs stored on a remote NFS export cannot be run on this machine. Not applicable if the system has no NFS mounts.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231070.caution: If users or applications legitimately run binaries or scripts from an NFS share, adding noexec will break that; confirm what lives on each export before changing the mount options.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231075.summary: Every NFS mount listed in /etc/fstab must carry the nosuid option so that setuid or setgid programs on a remote export cannot gain elevated privileges on this machine. Not applicable if the system has no NFS mounts.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231075.caution: Any setuid program that is expected to run from the NFS share will silently lose its elevated privileges after this change.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231080.summary: Any /etc/fstab entry for removable media (USB sticks, optical drives, and the like) must include the noexec option so that programs on plugged-in media cannot be executed directly.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231080.caution: Deciding which fstab entries refer to removable media is a judgment call, and installers or tools run from removable media will stop working.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231085.summary: Any /etc/fstab entry for removable media must include the nodev option so that device files carried on plugged-in media are not honored by the kernel.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231085.caution: Identifying which fstab entries refer to removable media requires a human look at the file; the option itself rarely breaks anything.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231090.summary: Any /etc/fstab entry for removable media must include the nosuid option so that setuid or setgid programs on plugged-in media cannot run with elevated privileges.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231090.caution: Identifying which fstab entries refer to removable media requires a human look at the file; the option itself rarely breaks anything.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231095.summary: The /boot file system must be mounted with the nodev option so that no device files placed there are treated as real devices. Edit the /boot line in /etc/fstab to add the option.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231095.caution: A typo in the /etc/fstab line for /boot can prevent the system from booting, so double-check the edit and keep a way to boot into rescue mode.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231100.summary: The /boot file system must be mounted with the nosuid option so that setuid or setgid programs cannot run from it. Edit the /boot line in /etc/fstab to add the option.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231100.caution: A typo in the /etc/fstab line for /boot can prevent the system from booting, so double-check the edit and keep a way to boot into rescue mode.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231105.summary: On UEFI systems, the /boot/efi file system must be mounted with the nosuid option so that setuid or setgid programs cannot run from it. Not applicable to BIOS systems, and the note says it does not apply to vfat file systems.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231105.caution: The check text both shows a vfat example and says the control is not applicable to vfat; since /boot/efi is normally vfat, decide with your assessor how to treat this before editing /etc/fstab.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231110.summary: The shared-memory file system /dev/shm must be mounted with the nodev option so device files cannot be created there. Add the option in /etc/fstab, reload systemd, and remount /dev/shm.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231110.caution: If /dev/shm has no /etc/fstab line yet you must add one rather than edit; a malformed entry can cause the mount to fail on reboot.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231115.summary: The shared-memory file system /dev/shm must be mounted with the noexec option so programs cannot be executed from it. Add the option in /etc/fstab, reload systemd, and remount /dev/shm.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231115.caution: Some applications place executable code or JIT-compiled objects in /dev/shm and will fail with noexec set; test with your workloads first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231120.summary: The shared-memory file system /dev/shm must be mounted with the nosuid option so setuid or setgid programs cannot run from it. Add the option in /etc/fstab, reload systemd, and remount /dev/shm.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231120.caution: If /dev/shm has no /etc/fstab line yet you must add one rather than edit; a malformed entry can cause the mount to fail on reboot.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231125.summary: The /tmp file system must be mounted with the nodev option so device files cannot be created in the temporary directory. Add the option to the /tmp line in /etc/fstab.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231125.caution: This only works if /tmp is a separate mount; if it is just a directory on the root file system there is no fstab line to change.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231130.summary: The /tmp file system must be mounted with the noexec option so that programs downloaded or unpacked into /tmp cannot be run. Add the option to the /tmp line in /etc/fstab.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231130.caution: Many installers, package scripts, and build tools execute helpers from /tmp and will fail with noexec set; test before applying to production systems.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231135.summary: The /tmp file system must be mounted with the nosuid option so setuid or setgid programs cannot run from the temporary directory. Add the option to the /tmp line in /etc/fstab.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231135.caution: This only works if /tmp is a separate mount; if it is just a directory on the root file system there is no fstab line to change.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231140.summary: The /var file system must be mounted with the nodev option so device files cannot be created under /var. Add the option to the /var line in /etc/fstab.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231140.caution: This requires /var to be its own partition; on systems where it is part of the root file system there is nothing to edit and the finding must be handled differently.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231145.summary: The /var/log file system must be mounted with the nodev option so device files cannot be created in the log directory. Add the option to the /var/log line in /etc/fstab.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231145.caution: This requires /var/log to be its own partition; if it is not, there is no fstab line to modify.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231150.summary: The /var/log file system must be mounted with the noexec option so programs cannot be executed from the log directory. Add the option to the /var/log line in /etc/fstab.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231150.caution: This requires /var/log to be its own partition; if it is not, there is no fstab line to modify.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231155.summary: The /var/log file system must be mounted with the nosuid option so setuid or setgid programs cannot run from the log directory. Add the option to the /var/log line in /etc/fstab.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231155.caution: This requires /var/log to be its own partition; if it is not, there is no fstab line to modify.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231160.summary: The /var/log/audit file system must be mounted with the nodev option so device files cannot be created in the audit log directory. Add the option to the /var/log/audit line in /etc/fstab.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231160.caution: This requires /var/log/audit to be its own partition; if it is not, there is no fstab line to modify.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231165.summary: The /var/log/audit file system must be mounted with the noexec option so programs cannot be executed from the audit log directory. Add the option to the /var/log/audit line in /etc/fstab.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231165.caution: This requires /var/log/audit to be its own partition; if it is not, there is no fstab line to modify.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231170.summary: The /var/log/audit file system must be mounted with the nosuid option so setuid or setgid programs cannot run from the audit log directory. Add the option to the /var/log/audit line in /etc/fstab.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231170.caution: This requires /var/log/audit to be its own partition; if it is not, there is no fstab line to modify.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231175.summary: The /var/tmp file system must be mounted with the nodev option so device files cannot be created there. Add the option to the /var/tmp line in /etc/fstab.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231175.caution: This requires /var/tmp to be its own partition; if it is not, there is no fstab line to modify.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231180.summary: The /var/tmp file system must be mounted with the noexec option so programs cannot be executed from it. Add the option to the /var/tmp line in /etc/fstab.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231180.caution: Some software runs helper scripts from /var/tmp and will fail with noexec set; test with your applications before applying.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231185.summary: The /var/tmp file system must be mounted with the nosuid option so setuid or setgid programs cannot run from it. Add the option to the /var/tmp line in /etc/fstab.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231185.caution: This requires /var/tmp to be its own partition; if it is not, there is no fstab line to modify.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231200.summary: Every local disk partition other than the root file system must be mounted with the nodev option, so an attacker cannot create fake device files on a data partition and use them to reach hardware. Set the option in /etc/fstab for each non-root local partition.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231200.caution: Do not add nodev to a partition that genuinely holds device files, such as a chroot or container root, or software inside it will break.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232010.summary: No program in the standard system command directories (/bin, /sbin, /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /usr/libexec, and the local equivalents) may be writable by its group or by everyone, so that an ordinary user cannot replace a command that administrators run.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232010.caution: Because the check follows symbolic links, it can flag targets outside the listed directories; review the output before changing permissions in bulk.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232015.summary: The system-wide shared library directories (/lib, /lib64, /usr/lib, /usr/lib64) must not be writable by group or others, so nobody can slip a malicious library into a place every program loads from.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232020.summary: Shared library files (*.so*) under /lib, /lib64, /usr/lib, and /usr/lib64 must be mode 0755 or tighter, so nobody without root can modify code that gets loaded into every process. The fix removes group and world write bits from any offending file.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232025.summary: The /var/log directory itself must be mode 0755 or tighter, so only root can create or delete log files there and ordinary users cannot tamper with what gets logged.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232030.summary: The main system log file /var/log/messages must be mode 0640 or tighter, so ordinary users cannot read log entries that may reveal sensitive details about the system and other users.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232030.caution: Log rotation may recreate the file with a different mode, so check the logrotate configuration as well if the finding keeps reappearing.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232035.summary: The audit tools (auditctl, aureport, ausearch, autrace, auditd, rsyslogd, augenrules under /sbin) must be mode 0755 or tighter, so non-root users cannot alter the programs that record and report on security events.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232040.summary: The owner, group, and permissions of the cron configuration files and directories must match what the cronie and crontabs packages shipped. If they have drifted, reinstall the packages and reset ownership and permissions from the package database.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232040.caution: Reinstalling the packages restores default permissions but may also overwrite locally customized config files if they are not marked as config in the package; back up /etc/cron.* first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232045.summary: Hidden startup files in user home directories (such as shell profile files) must be mode 0740 or tighter, so other users cannot read or edit the commands that run when someone logs in.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232045.caution: The fix is shown per file, so applying it across all home directories needs a loop; some hidden files are data rather than scripts and tightening them is harmless but may surprise users.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232050.summary: Each local interactive user's home directory must be mode 0750 or tighter, so other users cannot browse into it. Change the mode of any home directory that is more open.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232050.caution: Tightening a home directory can break setups where other users or services deliberately read from it, such as shared web content or public SSH keys, so check for such use first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232055.summary: The /etc/group file must be mode 0644 or tighter so that only root can change group membership definitions.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232060.summary: The backup copy /etc/group- must be mode 0644 or tighter so that only root can modify it; the backup carries the same sensitive group data as the live file.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232065.summary: The /etc/gshadow file, which holds group passwords, must be mode 0000 so that nobody other than root (which bypasses permissions) can read or write it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232070.summary: The backup copy /etc/gshadow- must be mode 0000 so that nobody other than root can read the group password data it contains.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232075.summary: The /etc/passwd file must be mode 0644 or tighter so that only root can change user account definitions.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232080.summary: The backup copy /etc/passwd- must be mode 0644 or tighter so that only root can modify it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232085.summary: The backup copy /etc/shadow- must be mode 0000 so that nobody other than root can read the password hashes it contains.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232090.summary: The /etc/group file must be owned by root so that no other account can rewrite group membership.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232095.summary: The /etc/group file must have root as its group owner so that group permissions on the file do not hand write access to a non-root group.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232100.summary: The backup copy /etc/group- must be owned by root so that no other account can tamper with it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232103.summary: The /etc/audit/ directory, which holds the audit daemon's configuration and rules, must be owned by root so that no other account can change what gets audited.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232104.summary: The /etc/audit/ directory must have root as its group owner so that a non-root group cannot gain access to audit configuration through group permissions.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232105.summary: The backup copy /etc/group- must have root as its group owner so that a non-root group cannot modify it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232110.summary: The /etc/gshadow file, which holds group passwords, must be owned by root so that no other account can read or change it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232115.summary: The /etc/gshadow file must have root as its group owner so that group permissions cannot expose group password data to a non-root group.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232120.summary: The backup copy /etc/gshadow- must be owned by root so that no other account can read the group password data it contains.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232125.summary: The backup copy /etc/gshadow- must have root as its group owner so that a non-root group cannot access it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232130.summary: The /etc/passwd file must be owned by root so that no other account can add, remove, or alter user accounts.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232135.summary: The /etc/passwd file must have root as its group owner so that a non-root group cannot gain write access to account definitions.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232140.summary: The backup copy /etc/passwd- must be owned by root so that no other account can tamper with it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232145.summary: The backup copy /etc/passwd- must have root as its group owner so that a non-root group cannot modify it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232150.summary: The /etc/shadow file, which holds the password hashes, must be owned by root so that no other account can read or change them.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232155.summary: The /etc/shadow file must have root as its group owner so that group permissions cannot expose password hashes to a non-root group.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232160.summary: The backup copy /etc/shadow- must be owned by root so that no other account can read the password hashes it contains.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232165.summary: The backup copy /etc/shadow- must have root as its group owner so that a non-root group cannot access the password hashes it contains.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232170.summary: The /var/log directory must be owned by root so that only root controls which log files exist and can be created or removed there.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232175.summary: The /var/log directory must have root as its group owner so that a non-root group cannot gain control over the log directory through group permissions.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232180.summary: The main system log /var/log/messages must be owned by root so that no other account can alter or erase the log entries.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232185.summary: The main system log /var/log/messages must have root as its group owner so that a non-root group cannot read or modify it through group permissions.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232190.summary: Every program in the standard system command directories (/bin, /sbin, /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /usr/libexec, and the local equivalents) must be owned by root, so no other account can replace a command that administrators and services run.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232190.caution: The check follows symbolic links, so a link pointing to a file elsewhere may be flagged; review what is listed before changing ownership.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232195.summary: Every program in the standard system command directories must be group-owned by root or a required system account, so a group that ordinary users belong to cannot modify system commands.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232195.caution: Some commands are deliberately group-owned by a service account; changing them to root can break that service, so confirm which system groups are required before applying the fix.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232200.summary: Shared library files (*.so*) under /lib, /lib64, /usr/lib, and /usr/lib64 must be owned by root, so no other account can substitute code that gets loaded into every process. The fix reassigns any offending file to root.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232205.summary: Shared library files under /lib, /lib64, /usr/lib, and /usr/lib64 must be group-owned by root or a required system account, so no ordinary group can modify code loaded by every program. The fix changes the group of any offending file to root.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232205.caution: The title allows a system account as group owner but the fix blindly sets root; check whether any flagged library is intentionally group-owned by a service account first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232210.summary: The shared library directories under /lib, /lib64, /usr/lib, and /usr/lib64 must be owned by root so no other account can add or replace libraries there.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232215.summary: The shared library directories under /lib, /lib64, /usr/lib, and /usr/lib64 must be group-owned by root or a required system account, so ordinary groups cannot add or replace libraries.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232215.caution: Confirm that any directory flagged is not intentionally group-owned by a required system account before changing it to root.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232220.summary: The audit tools (auditctl, aureport, ausearch, autrace, auditd, rsyslogd, augenrules under /sbin) must be owned by root so no other account can tamper with the programs that record and report security events.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232225.summary: The audit tools under /sbin must be group-owned by root so a non-root group cannot modify the programs that record and report security events.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232230.summary: All cron configuration files and directories under /etc (crontab, cron.d, cron.daily, and the rest) must be owned by root, so no other account can schedule jobs that run with system privileges.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232235.summary: All cron configuration files and directories under /etc must be group-owned by root, so a non-root group cannot edit scheduled jobs that run with system privileges.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232240.summary: Any directory that everyone can write to must be owned by root, a system account, or an approved application account, not by an ordinary user, so a user cannot control a shared drop-off location. The check lists world-writable directories owned by non-system UIDs.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232240.caution: Deciding whether an owner counts as an approved application account is a human call, and changing ownership of a directory an application relies on can break that application.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232245.summary: Every world-writable directory must have the sticky bit set, so users can only delete or rename files they own even though anyone can create files there. Set the sticky bit on any directory the check lists.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232245.caution: The search walks the entire file system including network mounts and can take a long time; run it during a quiet period.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232250.summary: No file or directory on local file systems may belong to a group ID that no longer exists in the group database. Either delete such files or assign them a valid group, since orphaned group IDs can be silently inherited by a newly created group.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232250.caution: Orphaned files are often leftovers from removed accounts or software; check what they are before deleting or reassigning them, since a future group with the same ID would inherit access.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232255.summary: No file or directory on local file systems may belong to a user ID that no longer exists in the account database. Either delete such files or assign them a valid owner, since a new account given the same ID would inherit them.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232255.caution: Orphaned files are often leftovers from removed accounts; check what they contain before deleting them or handing them to another user.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232260.summary: All device files under /dev must carry a specific SELinux label rather than the generic device_t or unlabeled_t, so SELinux can actually restrict who touches each device. Relabel any flagged device from policy, or reinstall the package that provides support for that device class.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232260.caution: Some device files such as /dev/vmci on virtual machine hosts legitimately use device_t and are not findings, and a relabel that finds no more specific type means the SELinux policy itself must be extended.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-232270.summary: The /etc/shadow file, which holds every account's password hash, must be mode 0000 so that nobody other than root (which bypasses permissions) can read or write it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-251010.summary: The firewalld package must be installed so the system has a host firewall available to control which network connections are accepted.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-251010.caution: Installing the package alone does not change traffic; enabling and configuring the firewall afterward is what can block services, so plan the rules before turning it on.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-251015.summary: The firewalld service must be running so the host firewall is actually filtering network traffic, not merely installed. Enable and start it with systemctl.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-251015.caution: Starting the firewall with its default zone can immediately block services that clients depend on and can cut off remote access if ssh is not allowed; add the needed exceptions first or have console access ready.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-251020.summary: The firewall must default to dropping all inbound connections and allow only the services the mission needs. Add the required exceptions (for example ssh) to the drop zone, make drop the default zone, and assign the network interfaces to it.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-251020.caution: Switching the default zone to drop before adding the ssh exception will lock you out of a remote system; do the exceptions first and keep console access available.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-251030.summary: firewalld must use nftables as its backend so that connection rate limits can be applied to network interfaces, and rate-limiting rules for the organization-defined denial-of-service scenarios must then be established.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-251030.caution: Changing the firewall backend affects how existing rules are implemented and requires a firewalld restart, and the actual rate-limiting rules depend on what your organization has defined.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-251035.summary: The services, ports, and protocols allowed through the firewall must match the site's PPSM Component Local Service Assessment and must not include anything prohibited by the PPSM Category Assignments List. Compare the active firewall zones against the approved list and remove anything extra.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-251035.caution: Removing a firewall service or port that a real workload uses will break it; reconcile the PPSM list with what the system actually needs before reloading the rules.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-251040.summary: Network interfaces must not run in promiscuous mode, where they capture all traffic on the wire, unless the ISSO has approved and documented that use. Turn promiscuous mode off on any interface found using it.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-251040.caution: Packet-capture tools, intrusion detection sensors, and some virtual bridges legitimately need promiscuous mode; turning it off can silently break them, and the change made with the ip command is not persistent across reboots.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-251045.summary: The kernel parameter net.core.bpf_jit_harden must be set to 2 so the BPF just-in-time compiler applies its hardening to all users, making it harder to abuse JIT-compiled code for attacks. Set it in a drop-in file under /etc/sysctl.d and reload.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-251045.caution: Full JIT hardening can slightly reduce the performance of BPF-heavy workloads such as high-throughput packet filtering or tracing.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252010.summary: The chrony package must be installed so the system has a time synchronization client, which keeps clocks accurate enough for logs, authentication, and certificates to be trusted.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252015.summary: The chronyd time-synchronization service must be enabled and running so the system clock stays in step with the authoritative time source.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252015.caution: If another time client such as ntpd is already running, the two will conflict; use only one.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252020.summary: The /etc/chrony.conf file must point at an authoritative DOD time source and set maxpoll to 16 or less, so the clock is compared with the reference at least once every 24 hours.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252020.caution: Deciding which server counts as an authoritative DOD time source depends on your network, and pointing at an unreachable server will leave the clock drifting.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252035.summary: If the system uses DNS, at least two name servers must be configured (in /etc/resolv.conf or through the NetworkManager connection, depending on the DNS mode) so name resolution keeps working when one resolver is down. Not applicable when a cloud provider supplies a single highly available DNS address.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252035.caution: Edits to /etc/resolv.conf are overwritten by NetworkManager unless its DNS mode is set to none, so make the change in the right place for how the system is managed.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252040.summary: Give NetworkManager an explicit DNS processing mode (default, none, or systemd-resolved) in its configuration file, so the system's DNS handling is deliberate and documented rather than left to whatever behavior happens to apply.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252040.caution: Picking the wrong mode can change how /etc/resolv.conf is managed and break name resolution; if another DNS resolver is in use, document it with the ISSO instead.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252045.summary: Check whether the IPsec service is running and, if so, review every configured connection in /etc/ipsec.conf and /etc/ipsec.d/; any tunnel that is not approved and documented with the ISSO must be removed, since unauthorized tunnels can carry traffic around your network controls.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252045.caution: Removing a tunnel that is actually in use will cut off whatever traffic depends on it; confirm each connection's purpose before deleting it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252050.summary: If postfix is installed, restrict the mail server so it only relays mail for the local network and rejects everyone else; otherwise the host can be abused as an open relay for spam.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252050.caution: Any legitimate outside hosts that relay through this server will be rejected unless they are added to the restriction list and documented with the ISSO.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252060.summary: Add an alias in /etc/aliases so mail addressed to postmaster is delivered to root, and rebuild the alias database, so administrators actually receive notifications such as audit processing failures.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252060.caution: This only works if someone actually reads root's mail; the check also accepts other documented ways of notifying the administrator and ISSO.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252065.summary: Install the libreswan package if the system has an operational need for IPsec VPN tunnels; if there is no such need, the rule does not apply.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252065.caution: Installing it where it is not needed adds an unused service; decide first whether the system actually requires Libreswan.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253010.summary: Turn on TCP syncookies through a sysctl setting so the system can keep accepting connections during a SYN flood instead of exhausting its connection queue.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253015.summary: Set the kernel to ignore incoming IPv4 ICMP redirect messages on all interfaces, so an attacker on the network cannot use redirects to change the system's routing table.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253015.caution: If the system relies on router redirects to learn routes (unusual), it will need those routes configured statically.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253020.summary: Set the kernel to drop IPv4 source-routed packets on all interfaces, since source routing lets a sender dictate the path a packet takes and bypass normal routing controls.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253025.summary: Set the kernel to log IPv4 packets that arrive with impossible (martian) source addresses on all interfaces, giving you evidence of spoofing or misconfiguration on the network.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253025.caution: On a noisy network this can add a large volume of kernel log messages.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253030.summary: Set the default kernel setting so newly created IPv4 interfaces also log packets with impossible (martian) source addresses, so the logging applies to interfaces added later.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253030.caution: On a noisy network this can add a large volume of kernel log messages.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253035.summary: Enable reverse path filtering on all IPv4 interfaces so the kernel discards packets whose source address could not have arrived on that interface, which blocks many spoofed packets.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253035.caution: Strict reverse path filtering can drop legitimate traffic on hosts with asymmetric routing or multiple interfaces on different networks.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253040.summary: Set the default kernel setting so newly created IPv4 interfaces also ignore ICMP redirect messages, closing the gap for interfaces that appear after boot.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253045.summary: Set the default kernel setting so newly created IPv4 interfaces also drop source-routed packets, extending the protection to interfaces added after boot.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253050.summary: Set the default kernel setting so newly created IPv4 interfaces also use reverse path filtering, discarding packets whose source address could not have arrived on that interface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253050.caution: Reverse path filtering can drop legitimate traffic on hosts with asymmetric routing or multiple interfaces on different networks.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253055.summary: Set the kernel to ignore ICMP echo (ping) requests sent to a broadcast address, so the system cannot be used as an amplifier in a smurf-style denial-of-service attack.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253060.summary: Set the kernel to ignore bogus ICMP error responses rather than logging each one, so malformed or malicious ICMP traffic cannot fill the logs.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253065.summary: Set the kernel so the system does not send IPv4 ICMP redirect messages on any interface; only a router should tell other hosts to change their routes, and this must be documented with the ISSO if it is needed.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253065.caution: If this host genuinely acts as a router, sending redirects may be an operational requirement that should be documented with the ISSO instead.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253070.summary: Set the default kernel setting so newly created interfaces also do not send IPv4 ICMP redirect messages, unless the need is documented with the ISSO.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253070.caution: If this host genuinely acts as a router, sending redirects may be an operational requirement that should be documented with the ISSO instead.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253075.summary: Disable IPv4 packet forwarding in the kernel unless the system is a router and that role is documented with the ISSO, so the host does not silently pass traffic between networks.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-253075.caution: Turning off forwarding will break any host that routes, runs NAT, or hosts containers or virtual machines whose networking depends on forwarding; confirm the system's role first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-254010.summary: Set the kernel to ignore IPv6 router advertisements on all interfaces unless the system is a router, so a rogue device on the network cannot hand the host new addresses or routes. Not applicable if IPv6 is disabled.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-254010.caution: Hosts that rely on router advertisements for IPv6 addressing will lose automatic address and route configuration and need static IPv6 settings instead.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-254015.summary: Set the kernel to ignore incoming IPv6 ICMP redirect messages on all interfaces, so an attacker on the network cannot change the system's routing table. Not applicable if IPv6 is disabled.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-254020.summary: Set the kernel to drop IPv6 source-routed packets on all interfaces, since source routing lets a sender dictate the path a packet takes and bypass normal routing controls. Not applicable if IPv6 is disabled.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-254025.summary: Disable IPv6 packet forwarding in the kernel unless the system is a router, so the host does not pass traffic between networks. Not applicable if IPv6 is disabled.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-254025.caution: Turning off forwarding will break any host that routes IPv6 or hosts containers or virtual machines whose networking depends on it; confirm the system's role first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-254030.summary: Set the default kernel setting so newly created IPv6 interfaces also ignore router advertisements unless the system is a router. Not applicable if IPv6 is disabled.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-254030.caution: Hosts that rely on router advertisements for IPv6 addressing will lose automatic address and route configuration on new interfaces.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-254035.summary: Set the default kernel setting so newly created IPv6 interfaces also ignore ICMP redirect messages. Not applicable if IPv6 is disabled.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-254040.summary: Set the default kernel setting so newly created IPv6 interfaces also drop source-routed packets. Not applicable if IPv6 is disabled.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255010.summary: Install the openssh-server package so networked systems have an encrypted, authenticated way to be administered remotely.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255015.summary: Make sure the sshd service is enabled and running, so remote administration and file transfer happen over an encrypted, integrity-protected channel rather than something in the clear.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255020.summary: Install the openssh-clients package so the system has the standard tools for making encrypted connections and transfers to other hosts.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255025.summary: Configure the SSH server's Banner setting (in sshd_config or a file under sshd_config.d) to point at a file containing the DOD Notice and Consent Banner, so every SSH user sees the legal notice before logging in.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255025.caution: The banner file itself must contain the exact mandated text; pointing Banner at a missing or wrong file leaves the requirement unmet.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255030.summary: Set the SSH server's LogLevel to VERBOSE and restart sshd, so connection attempts and failures are recorded in enough detail to investigate break-in attempts.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255030.caution: Verbose logging increases the volume of SSH log entries, so make sure log storage and forwarding can absorb it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255035.summary: Set PubkeyAuthentication to yes in the SSH server configuration so users can authenticate with keys or smart cards instead of passwords alone; not applicable if an approved alternate multifactor method is in use.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255045.summary: Set PermitRootLogin to no in the SSH server configuration so nobody can log in remotely as root directly; administrators must log in as themselves and then escalate, which keeps actions attributable.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255045.caution: If root is the only account with SSH access (common on cloud images or appliances), applying this locks out remote administration; create and test a named administrator account first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255080.summary: Set HostbasedAuthentication to no in the SSH server configuration so a user cannot be trusted merely because they are connecting from a particular host; each login must present its own credentials.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255080.caution: Any workflow that depends on host-based trust between machines will stop working and must switch to key-based or other per-user authentication.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255085.summary: Set PermitUserEnvironment to no in the SSH server configuration so users cannot inject environment variables through their authorized_keys or environment files, which could otherwise be used to alter how programs run at login.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255085.caution: Users or automation relying on custom SSH environment settings will lose them and need another way to set those variables.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255090.summary: Set RekeyLimit in the SSH server configuration so session keys are renegotiated after a maximum amount of data (1G) and time (1h), limiting how much traffic is exposed if a single session key is compromised.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255095.summary: Set ClientAliveCountMax to 1 in the SSH server configuration so a connection is dropped after a single missed keepalive response; this works together with RHEL-09-255100 to close sessions whose client has gone silent.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255095.caution: Combined with the interval setting, clients on flaky links may be disconnected more readily; long-running unattended sessions should use keepalives or a terminal multiplexer.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255100.summary: Set ClientAliveInterval to 600 or less in the SSH server configuration so the server checks on idle clients every 10 minutes and, together with RHEL-09-255095, drops connections that have become unresponsive.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255100.caution: Sessions with no client response for 10 minutes will be terminated, which can surprise users with long-running interactive work on unstable networks.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255105.summary: Make sure /etc/ssh/sshd_config, the sshd_config.d directory, and every file inside it are group-owned by root, so no other group can modify the SSH server's configuration.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255105.caution: The fix command as written does not recurse into sshd_config.d, so check the individual files inside the directory as well.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255110.summary: Make sure /etc/ssh/sshd_config, the sshd_config.d directory, and every file inside it are owned by root, so only root can change how the SSH server behaves.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255115.summary: Verify with the package manager that the OpenSSH server's files still have the ownership and permissions they shipped with, and restore them if anything has drifted, so nobody has loosened access to the SSH configuration.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255115.caution: Restoring package defaults will overwrite any deliberate ownership or permission changes made to OpenSSH server files.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255120.summary: Make sure the SSH private host key files in /etc/ssh are readable only by their owner (mode 0600 or tighter), since anyone who can read them can impersonate the server.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255125.summary: Make sure the SSH public host key files in /etc/ssh are not writable by anyone but their owner (mode 0644 or tighter), so they cannot be swapped out. Public key files may live elsewhere depending on the installation.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255135.summary: Set GSSAPIAuthentication to no in the SSH server configuration unless GSSAPI logins are documented with the ISSO, reducing the authentication methods an attacker can probe.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255135.caution: Environments that use GSSAPI (Kerberos-style) single sign-on for SSH will lose that login method; document it with the ISSO instead if it is required.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255140.summary: Set KerberosAuthentication to no in the SSH server configuration unless Kerberos logins are documented with the ISSO, keeping unneeded authentication methods turned off.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255140.caution: Users who log in with Kerberos passwords over SSH will be unable to; document the need with the ISSO if it is an operational requirement.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255145.summary: Set IgnoreRhosts to yes in the SSH server configuration so the old .rhosts and .shosts trust files are ignored and cannot grant logins without proper credentials.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255150.summary: Set IgnoreUserKnownHosts to yes in the SSH server configuration so a user's personal known_hosts file cannot be used as a basis for host-based trust during authentication.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255155.summary: Set X11forwarding to no in the SSH server configuration so remote graphical applications cannot be tunneled through SSH, unless X11 forwarding is documented with the ISSO as an operational requirement.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255155.caution: Users who run graphical tools over SSH will lose that ability; document the need with the ISSO if it is required.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255160.summary: Set StrictModes to yes in the SSH server configuration so sshd refuses to use a user's key and configuration files if their home directory or those files are writable by others.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255160.caution: Users whose home directory or .ssh files have loose permissions will be unable to log in with keys until the permissions are tightened.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255165.summary: Set PrintLastLog to yes in the SSH server configuration so each user sees the date and time of their last login and can notice if someone else has used their account.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-255175.summary: Set X11UseLocalhost to yes in the SSH server configuration so any forwarded X display listens only on the loopback address and remote hosts cannot connect to it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271010.summary: On systems with the GNOME desktop, enable the login-screen banner in the system-wide dconf database and update it, so the DOD Notice and Consent Banner appears before anyone logs in graphically. Not applicable without a graphical interface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271010.caution: Enabling the banner is only half the job; the banner text itself must also be configured or users will see an empty notice.
