claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271015.summary: On GNOME systems, add a dconf lock for the login-screen banner-message-enable key so ordinary users cannot switch the logon banner off. Not applicable without a graphical interface.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271020.summary: On GNOME systems, set automount-open to false in the system dconf database so removable media are not mounted automatically when inserted, unless automounting is documented with the ISSO as an operational requirement. Not applicable without a graphical interface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271020.caution: Desktop users will have to mount USB drives and discs by hand, which may surprise them; document the need with the ISSO if automounting is required.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271025.summary: On GNOME systems, add a dconf lock for the automount-open key so users cannot turn automatic mounting of removable media back on. Not applicable without a graphical interface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271025.caution: If the system uses a dconf database other than local, the lock must be placed under that database's directory instead.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271030.summary: On GNOME systems, set autorun-never to true in the system dconf database so programs on removable media never start automatically when the media is inserted, unless documented with the ISSO. Not applicable without a graphical interface.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271035.summary: On GNOME systems, add a dconf lock for the autorun-never key so users cannot re-enable autorun for removable media. Not applicable without a graphical interface.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271045.summary: On GNOME systems, configure the smart card removal-action to lock-screen, either through an authselect profile with the with-smartcard-lock-on-removal feature or directly in the system dconf database, so pulling the smart card immediately locks the session. Not applicable without a graphical interface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271045.caution: Switching authselect profiles rewrites the PAM and nsswitch configuration; make sure smart card login already works before adding the lock-on-removal feature.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271050.summary: On GNOME systems, add a dconf lock for the smart card removal-action key so users cannot change what happens when they remove their card. Not applicable without a graphical interface.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271055.summary: On GNOME systems, set lock-enabled to true in the system dconf screensaver settings so the screen locks when the screensaver starts and the user must authenticate again to get back in. Not applicable without a graphical interface.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271060.summary: On GNOME systems, add a dconf lock for the screensaver lock-enabled key so users cannot disable screen locking for themselves. Not applicable without a graphical interface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271060.caution: If the system uses a dconf database other than local, the lock file must be created under that database's directory instead.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271065.summary: On GNOME systems, set the session idle-delay to 600 seconds or less (but not 0) in the system dconf database so an unattended desktop goes idle and locks after at most 10 minutes. Not applicable without a graphical interface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271065.caution: Users doing long read-only work such as monitoring displays will be locked out every 10 minutes unless an exception is arranged.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271070.summary: On GNOME systems, add a dconf lock for the session idle-delay key so users cannot lengthen or disable the inactivity timeout. Not applicable without a graphical interface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271070.caution: If the system uses a dconf database other than local, the lock file must be created under that database's directory instead.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271075.summary: On GNOME systems, set the screensaver lock-delay to 5 seconds or less in the system dconf database so the session locks almost immediately once the screensaver activates rather than leaving a window to walk back in. Not applicable without a graphical interface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271075.caution: The value must be written with the uint32 prefix exactly as shown or the setting is not applied.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271080.summary: On GNOME systems, add a dconf lock for the screensaver lock-delay key so users cannot delay or defeat the lock that follows screensaver activation. Not applicable without a graphical interface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271080.caution: If the system uses a dconf database other than local, the lock file must be created under that database's directory instead.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271085.summary: On GNOME systems, set the screensaver picture-uri to an empty value and lock it in dconf so the lock screen shows a blank image rather than a user-chosen picture that might reveal information. Not applicable without a graphical interface.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271090.summary: On GNOME systems, make sure the compiled dconf databases are newer than the keyfiles they are built from, and run the dconf update if not, so the security settings you wrote in the keyfiles are actually in effect. Not applicable without a graphical interface.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271095.summary: On GNOME systems, set disable-restart-buttons to true so the login screen offers no shutdown or restart buttons and someone without an account cannot reboot the machine. Not applicable without a graphical interface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271095.caution: The fix as written sets the value for the current user rather than in a system dconf keyfile; for a persistent system-wide setting it should be written to the dconf database.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271100.summary: On GNOME systems, add a dconf lock for the login-screen disable-restart-buttons key so users cannot bring the shutdown and restart buttons back. Not applicable without a graphical interface.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271105.summary: On GNOME systems, clear the media-keys logout binding so pressing Ctrl-Alt-Del in the desktop does not shut down or reboot the system by accident. Not applicable without a graphical interface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271105.caution: The fix as written sets the value for the current user rather than in a system dconf keyfile; for a persistent system-wide setting it should be written to the dconf database.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271110.summary: On GNOME systems, add a dconf lock for the media-keys logout key so users cannot re-enable the Ctrl-Alt-Del shortcut. Not applicable without a graphical interface.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271115.summary: On GNOME systems, set disable-user-list to true in the system dconf database so the login screen does not display account names, which would give an attacker half of a valid credential. Not applicable without a graphical interface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-271115.caution: Users will have to type their username at the login screen instead of clicking it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-291010.summary: Prevent the usb-storage kernel module from loading by blacklisting it in /etc/modprobe.d, so USB flash drives and disks cannot be used to copy data on or off the system unless the ISSO has documented a need.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-291010.caution: Any workflow that depends on USB drives (backups, media transfer, installation) will stop working; confirm the need and document it with the ISSO before applying.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-291015.summary: Install the usbguard package and enable its service so the system can block USB devices that are not on an approved list; not a finding on a virtual machine with no USB peripherals attached.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-291015.caution: Enabling usbguard before an allow list is configured immediately blocks USB keyboards and mice; configure the policy first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-291020.summary: Make sure the usbguard service is enabled and running so unauthorized USB peripherals are blocked before they connect; not a finding on a virtual machine with no USB peripherals attached.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-291020.caution: Starting usbguard without a properly configured policy immediately blocks USB keyboards and mice; confirm the rules file is in place first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-291030.summary: Give USBGuard a rules policy, typically generated from the USB devices currently attached, so only known peripherals are allowed and anything else is blocked before it connects. Not applicable on a virtual machine with no USB peripherals.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-291030.caution: Generate the policy while every legitimate device is plugged in; a device missing from the allow list, including the keyboard, will be blocked the moment usbguard starts.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-291035.summary: Prevent the bluetooth kernel module from loading by blacklisting it in /etc/modprobe.d and rebooting, so the system cannot be reached or leak data over Bluetooth unless the ISSO has documented a need.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-291035.caution: Bluetooth keyboards, mice, and headsets will stop working after the reboot; document the need with the ISSO if they are required.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-291040.summary: On machines with physical wireless radios, turn off all wireless interfaces unless the ISSO has documented and approved their use, so the system cannot be reached over an unmanaged radio link.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-291040.caution: If the machine's only network connection is wireless, turning the radios off disconnects it entirely, including any remote session you are using.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411010.summary: Set PASS_MAX_DAYS to 60 in /etc/login.defs so passwords for new accounts and future password changes expire after at most 60 days, limiting how long a stolen password stays useful.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411010.caution: This only affects accounts created or passwords changed afterward; existing accounts must be updated separately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411015.summary: Review every account in /etc/shadow and set a maximum password age of 60 days on any interactive account that has a longer or unlimited lifetime, so existing users are also forced to rotate passwords.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411015.caution: Users whose passwords are already older than 60 days will be forced to change them at next login; service accounts should be excluded or documented rather than expired.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411020.summary: Set CREATE_HOME to yes in /etc/login.defs so every new local interactive user automatically gets a home directory, avoiding users landing in a shared or root-level directory.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411025.summary: Search each local interactive user's initialization files for umask statements looser than 077 and remove them, so users' new files are private by default; application accounts needing a looser umask must be documented with the ISSO.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411025.caution: Removing a umask a user set deliberately can break shared-directory workflows that expect group-readable files; talk to the user or document the exception first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411030.summary: Find any interactive user accounts in /etc/passwd that share the same UID and give each one a unique UID, so file ownership and audit records can be tied to a single person.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411030.caution: Changing a user's UID does not update ownership of their existing files; those must be re-owned or the user loses access to their own data.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411035.summary: Give every system account (UID below 1000, other than root) a nologin shell so these service accounts cannot be used for interactive logins; any that need a shell must be documented with the ISSO.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411035.caution: Never change root's shell, as the fix text warns that doing so makes the system inaccessible; also confirm no service account actually needs a shell before changing it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411040.summary: Set an expiration date no more than 72 hours out on every temporary account so short-term access does not quietly become permanent.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411040.caution: Identifying which accounts are temporary is a human decision; expiring the wrong account cuts off a legitimate user.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411045.summary: Run the password file consistency check and fix any interactive user whose primary group ID in /etc/passwd does not exist in /etc/group, so file ownership and permissions behave predictably.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411045.caution: When fixing a user's GID, choose an existing group appropriate for that user rather than an arbitrary one, or the user may gain access to another group's files.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411050.summary: Set the default account inactivity period for new users to 35 days or less so an account whose password has expired and gone unused is automatically disabled instead of lingering as a target.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411050.caution: This default only applies to accounts created afterward; existing accounts are not changed by this setting.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411055.summary: Check each local interactive user's initialization files for PATH statements and remove any directory that is outside the user's home directory or the system default, unless the ISSO has documented the need; a stray directory in PATH lets planted programs run in place of real ones.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411055.caution: Editing a user's PATH can break tools they rely on; confirm what each extra directory is for before removing it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411060.summary: Make sure every local interactive user (normally UID 1000 or above with a real login shell) has a home directory defined in /etc/passwd, creating and assigning one where it is missing.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411065.summary: Make sure the home directory listed in /etc/passwd for every local interactive user actually exists on disk, creating any that are missing with the right owner, group, and 0750 permissions.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411065.caution: Set the owner and group correctly when creating the directory or the user will be unable to write to their own home.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411070.summary: Each local interactive user's home directory must be group-owned by that user's primary group as listed in /etc/passwd, so other groups cannot read the user's files and the user's own group can.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411070.caution: Changing the group owner of a home directory can break access for other users who were deliberately sharing files through the old group.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411075.summary: Configure faillock so an account is locked after three (or fewer) failed logon attempts, which blunts password-guessing attacks against local accounts.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411075.caution: Users who mistype their password a few times will be locked out and need an administrator to unlock them.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411080.summary: Apply the failed-logon lockout to the root account as well (the even_deny_root setting), so root cannot be brute-forced while every other account is protected.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411080.caution: An attacker or a misbehaving script can deliberately lock out root; make sure another way to reach the system exists before enabling this.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411085.summary: Set the faillock counting window to 900 seconds (15 minutes) so three failed logons within that period lock the account. Not applicable if an approved central account-management system already enforces this.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411085.caution: Combined with the deny and unlock settings, this will lock out legitimate users who fumble their password; plan for an unlock process.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411090.summary: Set unlock_time to 0 so a locked account stays locked until an administrator manually releases it, rather than unlocking itself after a timeout.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411090.caution: Every lockout, including accidental ones and root, now requires human intervention; without an out-of-band admin path a locked system may become unreachable.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411095.summary: Compare the local interactive accounts in /etc/passwd against the list of accounts the system administrator or ISSO has authorized, and delete any that are not on it, since unused accounts are extra ways in.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411095.caution: Deleting the wrong account can remove someone's access and their files; confirm the authorized list before removing anything.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411105.summary: Point faillock at a nondefault tally directory (the example is /var/log/faillock) so lockout counters survive a reboot and an attacker cannot reset them by rebooting.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411105.caution: The directory must exist with the correct SELinux context or lockouts may not be recorded at all.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411110.summary: Every group in /etc/group must have its own unique GID; duplicate GIDs make it impossible to tell groups apart for access control and accountability.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-411110.caution: Changing a group's GID does not update files owned by the old GID, so file ownership and access must be reviewed afterward.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-412035.summary: Set TMOUT to 600 or less in a script under /etc/profile.d so an idle interactive shell is closed after 10 minutes, reducing the chance an unattended terminal is hijacked.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-412035.caution: Long-running interactive work will be cut off after ten minutes of inactivity, which can surprise users running unattended sessions.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-412045.summary: Enable the audit option in faillock so the username is recorded whenever a logon attempt fails, giving investigators something to work with after an attack.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-412050.summary: Set FAIL_DELAY to 4 or more in /etc/login.defs so the system waits at least four seconds before offering another logon prompt after a failure, slowing down password guessing.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-412055.summary: Set the default umask to 077 in /etc/bashrc so new files created by bash users are readable and writable only by their owner.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-412055.caution: Files created after this change will not be readable by group members or others, which can break shared directories and scripts that expect looser permissions.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-412060.summary: Set the default umask to 077 in /etc/csh.cshrc so new files created by c shell users are readable and writable only by their owner.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-412060.caution: Files created after this change will not be readable by group members or others, which can break shared directories and scripts that expect looser permissions.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-412065.summary: Set UMASK to 077 in /etc/login.defs so the system-wide default for new files gives access only to the owner.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-412065.caution: Files created after this change will not be readable by group members or others, which can break shared directories and scripts that expect looser permissions.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-412070.summary: Set umask to 077 in /etc/profile so the system default profile gives new files owner-only permissions.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-412070.caution: Files created after this change will not be readable by group members or others, which can break shared directories and scripts that expect looser permissions.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-412080.summary: Configure systemd-logind with StopIdleSessionSec=600 (in a drop-in under /etc/systemd/logind.conf.d/) so login sessions idle for 10 minutes are terminated, then restart systemd-logind.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-412080.caution: Idle console and SSH sessions will be killed after ten minutes, which can interrupt users who leave work running in a session.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-431015.summary: Set SELINUXTYPE=targeted in /etc/selinux/config so SELinux confines network and system services that are likely attack targets; a reboot is needed for the change to apply.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-431015.caution: Switching SELinux policy types requires a reboot and a filesystem relabel, and can leave services unable to start if their contexts are wrong.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-431016.summary: Add a sudoers rule for the designated admin group that sets TYPE=sysadm_t ROLE=sysadm_r, so administrators using "sudo" get an elevated SELinux context rather than staying unconfined; remove conflicting entries from /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-431016.caution: A wrong sudoers entry or an SELinux role that the admin users are not allowed to enter can break "sudo" for every administrator; test on one account first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-431020.summary: When faillock uses a nondefault tally directory such as /var/log/faillock, label that directory with the faillog_t SELinux type so faillock can write to it under the targeted policy.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-431020.caution: If the context is not applied, faillock cannot record failures and account lockout silently stops working.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-431025.summary: Install the policycoreutils package, which provides the basic tools needed to manage and verify SELinux.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-431030.summary: Install the policycoreutils-python-utils package, which provides semanage, audit2allow, and related tools needed to manage SELinux policy.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-432010.summary: Install the sudo package so administrators can be given limited root privileges with logging instead of sharing the root password.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-432015.summary: Set timestamp_timeout=0 in /etc/sudoers (or one file in /etc/sudoers.d) so "sudo" asks for the password on every invocation instead of remembering it; the setting must appear in only one file.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-432015.caution: Administrators will be prompted for their password on every "sudo" command, which can break scripts that rely on a cached "sudo" session.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-432020.summary: Define Defaults !targetpw, !rootpw, and !runaspw in one sudoers file so "sudo" prompts for the invoking user's own password rather than the root or target user's password.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-432020.caution: If these appear in more than one file the check fails; consolidate them in a single location.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-432025.summary: Remove every !authenticate entry from /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d so no user can run privileged commands through "sudo" without authenticating.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-432025.caution: Service accounts or automation that relied on passwordless "sudo" via !authenticate will start failing and need another approach.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-432030.summary: Remove sudoers entries that grant ALL users the ability to run any command as any user (ALL ALL=(ALL) ALL and ALL ALL=(ALL:ALL) ALL), so only named people or groups can escalate privileges.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-432030.caution: Make sure at least one administrator still has a working "sudo" rule before removing the catch-all entries.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-432035.summary: Uncomment the pam_wheel.so use_uid line in /etc/pam.d/su so only members of the wheel group can use the su command; create the wheel group and add administrators if needed.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-432035.caution: Any administrator who is not in the wheel group loses the ability to su to root; add them to wheel before enabling this.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-433010.summary: Install the fapolicyd package, the application allow-listing tool that can restrict which programs are permitted to run.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-433015.summary: Enable and start the fapolicyd service so application allow-listing is actively enforced.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-433015.caution: Starting fapolicyd with an incomplete allow list can block legitimate programs and lock administrators out of their tools.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-433016.summary: Configure fapolicyd with permissive = 0 and a rule set whose final rule denies everything not explicitly allowed, so only authorized software can execute. Build the allow list in permissive mode first.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-433016.caution: Switching to enforcing mode before the allow list is complete can block essential binaries and make the system unusable; build and test the list in permissive mode first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611010.summary: Set retry = 3 in pwquality.conf so a user gets at most three attempts to pick an acceptable new password before the password change fails.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611030.summary: Make sure /etc/pam.d/system-auth loads pam_faillock.so with preauth (before pam_unix.so), authfail, and account lines, so failed-login lockout actually takes effect; with authselect this is done by enabling the with-faillock feature.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611030.caution: Editing PAM files by hand can break every login on the system if a line is wrong; keep a root session open while testing.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611035.summary: Make sure /etc/pam.d/password-auth loads pam_faillock.so with preauth (before pam_unix.so), authfail, and account lines, so failed-login lockout applies to remote and service logins; with authselect this is done by enabling the with-faillock feature.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611035.caution: Editing PAM files by hand can break every login on the system if a line is wrong; keep a root session open while testing.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611040.summary: Ensure /etc/pam.d/password-auth contains a password line using pam_pwquality.so so password complexity rules are enforced when passwords are changed through that stack.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611040.caution: A malformed PAM line can prevent password changes or logins; verify the file carefully after editing.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611045.summary: Ensure /etc/pam.d/system-auth contains a password line using pam_pwquality.so so password complexity rules are enforced when passwords are changed through that stack.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611045.caution: A malformed PAM line can prevent password changes or logins; verify the file carefully after editing.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611050.summary: In /etc/pam.d/password-auth, set the pam_unix.so password line to use sha512 with rounds=100000 so stored password hashes are much harder to crack.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611050.caution: Running authselect later will overwrite this setting unless a custom authselect profile is created, and more rounds make each password check slower.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611055.summary: In /etc/pam.d/system-auth, set the pam_unix.so password line to use sha512 with rounds=100000 so stored password hashes are much harder to crack.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611055.caution: Running authselect later will overwrite this setting unless a custom authselect profile is created, and more rounds make each password check slower.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611060.summary: Add enforce_for_root to pwquality.conf so the root account is held to the same password complexity rules as everyone else instead of being exempt.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611065.summary: Set lcredit = -1 in pwquality.conf so new passwords must contain at least one lowercase letter.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611070.summary: Set dcredit = -1 in pwquality.conf so new passwords must contain at least one digit.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611075.summary: Set PASS_MIN_DAYS to 1 or more in /etc/login.defs so newly created users cannot change their password again within 24 hours, which stops them cycling through passwords to defeat history checks.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611075.caution: This only affects accounts created after the change; existing accounts are covered by the separate /etc/shadow rule.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611080.summary: Check /etc/shadow for user accounts whose minimum password age is less than one day and set it to 1 for each, so users cannot immediately change a password back to a previous one.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611080.caution: System accounts are excluded; a user who just changed their password will be unable to change it again for a day.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611085.summary: Remove NOPASSWD from /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d so users must enter a password to escalate privileges, unless the ISSO has documented an MFA-backed admin group that is allowed to keep it.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611085.caution: Automation and service accounts that depend on passwordless "sudo" will break; identify and document approved exceptions before commenting out the entries.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611090.summary: Set minlen = 15 in pwquality.conf so new passwords must be at least 15 characters long.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611090.caution: Users with shorter existing passwords are not forced to change, but any new password they choose must meet the length.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611100.summary: Set ocredit = -1 in pwquality.conf so new passwords must contain at least one special character.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611105.summary: Set dictcheck to a nonzero value in pwquality.conf so new passwords are rejected if they are based on dictionary words.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611110.summary: Set ucredit = -1 in pwquality.conf so new passwords must contain at least one uppercase letter.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611115.summary: Set difok = 8 in pwquality.conf so a new password must differ from the old one in at least eight characters, preventing trivial one-character changes.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611120.summary: Set maxclassrepeat = 4 in pwquality.conf so a password cannot contain more than four consecutive characters of the same class (for example five digits in a row).

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611125.summary: Set maxrepeat = 3 in pwquality.conf so a password cannot contain the same character more than three times in a row.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611130.summary: Set minclass = 4 in pwquality.conf so new passwords must use all four character classes: uppercase, lowercase, digits, and special characters.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611135.summary: Set crypt_style = sha512 in the [defaults] section of /etc/libuser.conf so account-management utilities that use libuser hash passwords with SHA-512.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611140.summary: Set ENCRYPT_METHOD SHA512 in /etc/login.defs so passwords written to the shadow file are hashed with SHA-512 rather than a weaker algorithm.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611140.caution: Existing password hashes are not rehashed until each user next changes their password.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611145.summary: Remove any pam_succeed_if lines from /etc/pam.d/sudo so no group or condition lets users skip the password prompt when escalating privileges.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611145.caution: Anyone who was relying on that bypass will now be prompted for a password when using "sudo".

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611155.summary: Find accounts in /etc/shadow with an empty password field and either set a password or lock the account, because a blank password lets anyone log in as that user.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611155.caution: Locking an account that a service depends on can stop that service; check what each affected account is used for before locking it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611160.summary: Configure OpenSC to load the cac card driver and restart pcscd so DOD Common Access Cards are recognized for smart card login.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611160.caution: If smart card readers or other card types are in use, changing the driver list can prevent those cards from being read.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611165.summary: Set pam_cert_auth = True in the SSSD configuration so users can authenticate with the certificate on their smart card. Not applicable if an approved alternate multifactor method is in use.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611165.caution: Without a working certificate mapping and CA trust configured first, enabling certificate authentication can leave users unable to log in.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611170.summary: Add certificate_verification = ocsp_dgst=sha512 to the SSSD configuration (with root-only ownership and mode 600 on the file) so smart card certificates are checked for revocation via OCSP before login is allowed.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611170.caution: If the OCSP responder is unreachable from this host, certificate logins may fail; confirm network access to the responder first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611175.summary: Install the pcsc-lite package, which provides smart card reader support needed for multifactor authentication. Not applicable if an approved alternate MFA method is used.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611180.summary: Enable and start the pcscd socket so the smart card daemon is available when a card reader is used for authentication.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611185.summary: Install the opensc package, which provides the smart card tools and drivers needed for CAC and PIV authentication.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611190.summary: Every SSH private key stored on the system must be protected with a passphrase; keys that load without prompting for one must be replaced with new key pairs created with a passphrase. Not applicable if an approved alternate MFA method is used.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611190.caution: Replacing unprotected keys breaks any automated job or service that authenticates with them until the new keys are distributed and the old ones removed.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611195.summary: Ensure the systemd emergency.service uses systemd-sulogin-shell so booting into emergency mode requires the root password rather than dropping to an unauthenticated shell; the setting may live in the default unit or a drop-in, not both.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611195.caution: If the root password is lost or root is locked, emergency mode will no longer offer a way in without other recovery media.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611200.summary: Ensure the systemd rescue.service uses systemd-sulogin-shell so booting into single-user (rescue) mode requires the root password; the setting may live in the default unit or a drop-in, not both.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-611200.caution: If the root password is lost or root is locked, rescue mode will no longer offer a way in without other recovery media.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-631010.summary: For smart card login, install the DOD root CA chain (from the cyber.mil PKI bundle) into /etc/sssd/pki/sssd_auth_ca_db.pem so user certificates can be validated back to a trusted anchor. Not applicable if an approved alternate MFA method is used.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-631010.caution: An incomplete or outdated CA bundle will cause valid smart card logins to be rejected.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-631015.summary: Add a certmap section to the SSSD configuration that maps the certificate on a user's smart card to their account, so it is always clear which person authenticated; restart sssd afterward. Not applicable if an approved alternate MFA method is used.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-631015.caution: A wrong match or map rule can prevent users from logging in with their cards, or map them to the wrong account; the example rule must be adapted to your domain.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-631020.summary: If SSSD caches credentials (cache_credentials = true), set offline_credentials_expiration = 1 so cached logins stop working after one day and stale credentials cannot be reused indefinitely.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-631020.caution: Users on machines that are disconnected from the identity server for more than a day will be unable to log in.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-651010.summary: Install the AIDE file integrity tool and initialize its database so unauthorized changes to system files can be detected; another integrity tool is acceptable if the administrator can show how checks are done.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-651010.caution: Initializing the database takes time and disk space, and it must be taken from a known-good state or it will bless existing tampering.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-651015.summary: Schedule the file integrity tool (for example AIDE via a script in /etc/cron.daily) to run at least weekly and mail the results to designated personnel, so unauthorized changes to the baseline are noticed.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-651015.caution: Mail delivery must actually work for notifications to reach anyone, and a noisy baseline will generate reports nobody reads.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-651020.summary: Configure AIDE (or the file integrity tool in use) so every active selection rule in /etc/aide.conf includes sha512, using a FIPS 140-3 approved hash to detect file changes.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-651020.caution: Exclude log files and other frequently changing files from the rules or the integrity reports will be full of noise.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-651025.summary: Add lines to /etc/aide.conf that hash the audit tools (auditctl, auditd, ausearch, aureport, autrace, augenrules) with sha512 so tampering with them is detected.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-652010.summary: Install the rsyslog package so the system has a logging service capable of local and remote logging.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-652015.summary: Install the rsyslog-gnutls package so rsyslog can send logs to a remote server over TLS.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-652020.summary: Enable and start the rsyslog service so system logging is running.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-652025.summary: Unless this host is a documented log aggregation server, remove any rsyslog network listener configuration (imtcp, imudp, imrelp, or the legacy ServerRun directives) and restart rsyslog so it does not accept log messages from other machines.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-652025.caution: Removing listeners from a host that other systems actually send logs to will silently drop those logs; confirm the host's role first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-652030.summary: Configure rsyslog to log the auth, authpriv, and daemon facilities (the fix writes them to /var/log/secure) so all remote access activity is recorded; restart rsyslog afterward.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-652040.summary: Set $ActionSendStreamDriverAuthMode x509/name in the rsyslog configuration so the remote log server's certificate identity is verified before audit logs are sent to it.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-652040.caution: If the log server's certificate name does not match, log forwarding will stop; make sure the certificate and name are correct first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-652045.summary: Set $ActionSendStreamDriverMode 1 in the rsyslog configuration so audit records sent to a remote server are encrypted in transit.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-652045.caution: This requires the remote server to accept TLS connections, or log forwarding will fail.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-652050.summary: Set $DefaultNetstreamDriver gtls in the rsyslog configuration so rsyslog uses the GnuTLS driver to encrypt logs sent to a remote server.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-652050.caution: The rsyslog-gnutls package and valid certificates must be in place or rsyslog will fail to forward logs.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-652055.summary: Configure rsyslog to forward all logs over TCP to a remote log server, using either the legacy @@host:port syntax or an omfwd action, so audit records also exist somewhere other than the audited system.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-652055.caution: The remote server name, port, and network path must be correct and reachable or logs will queue up locally and never arrive.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-652060.summary: Configure rsyslog to log the cron facility (for example cron.* to /var/log/cron) so scheduled job execution can be traced and misuse of cron spotted; restart rsyslog afterward.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653010.summary: Install the audit package so the system can produce audit records of what happened, who did it, and when.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653015.summary: Enable and start the auditd service so audit records generated by the kernel are actually collected and written.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653020.summary: Set disk_error_action in /etc/audit/auditd.conf to HALT, SINGLE, or SYSLOG so the system reacts when it cannot write audit logs; HALT is the default expectation unless availability has been documented as more important with the ISSO.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653020.caution: With HALT, a disk error in the audit volume will shut the system down outright; choose SINGLE or SYSLOG only with a documented availability decision.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653025.summary: Set disk_full_action in /etc/audit/auditd.conf to HALT, SINGLE, or SYSLOG so the system reacts when the audit volume fills up; HALT is the default expectation unless availability has been documented as more important with the ISSO.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653025.caution: With HALT, a full audit partition will shut the system down; make sure log rotation and space alerts are in place before enabling it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653030.summary: Make sure the partition holding the audit log (see log_file in auditd.conf) is large enough for at least a week of audit records, typically around 10 GB, unless records are sent immediately to a central store.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653030.caution: Resizing or creating a partition is disruptive and may require downtime; size it based on the system's actual audit volume.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653035.summary: Set space_left = 25% in /etc/audit/auditd.conf so auditd triggers its warning action when the audit volume is 75 percent full, giving staff time to expand storage.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653040.summary: Set space_left_action = email in /etc/audit/auditd.conf so the SA and ISSO are notified when the audit volume reaches 75 percent full.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653040.caution: Local mail must be configured to reach a real mailbox or the alert goes nowhere.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653045.summary: Set admin_space_left = 5% in /etc/audit/auditd.conf so auditd takes its emergency action when the audit volume is 95 percent full, before auditing fails outright.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653050.summary: Set admin_space_left_action = single in /etc/audit/auditd.conf so the system drops to single-user mode when the audit volume reaches 95 percent full, then restart auditd.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653050.caution: When the threshold is hit the system leaves multi-user mode and stops serving users until an administrator intervenes at the console.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654165.summary: Add an audit rule that records every time a regular user runs the unix_update command, the privileged helper that writes password changes to the shadow file, so its use can be traced back to a person.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654165.caution: The rule must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654170.summary: Add an audit rule that records every time a regular user runs the userhelper command, a privileged helper for changing user account details, so its use can be traced back to a person.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654170.caution: The rule must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654175.summary: Add an audit rule that records every time a regular user runs the usermod command, so changes to user accounts can be traced back to a person.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654175.caution: The rule must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654180.summary: Add an audit rule that records every time a regular user runs the mount command, so attaching filesystems or removable media can be traced back to a person.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654180.caution: The rule must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654185.summary: Add an audit rule that records every time a regular user runs the init command, so attempts to change the system's run state can be traced back to a person.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654185.caution: The rule must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654190.summary: Add an audit rule that records every time a regular user runs the poweroff command, so attempts to shut the machine down can be traced back to a person.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654190.caution: The rule must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654195.summary: Add an audit rule that records every time a regular user runs the reboot command, so attempts to restart the machine can be traced back to a person.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654195.caution: The rule must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654200.summary: Add an audit rule that records every time a regular user runs the shutdown command, so attempts to halt or restart the machine can be traced back to a person.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654200.caution: The rule must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654205.summary: Add an audit rule that records any use of the 32-bit umount system call by a regular user, so unmounting of filesystems by 32-bit programs is logged and not just the umount command itself.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654205.caution: The rule must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654210.summary: Add audit rules that record any use of the umount2 system call by a regular user, for both 32-bit and 64-bit programs, so unmounting of filesystems by any program is logged.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654210.caution: Both the 32-bit and 64-bit rules are required and must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654215.summary: Add audit rules that record any write or attribute change to /etc/sudoers, so changes to who may run privileged commands are logged and can be tied to an account.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654215.caution: The rules must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654220.summary: Add audit rules that record any write or attribute change in the /etc/sudoers.d directory, so drop-in changes to privileged command access are logged and can be tied to an account.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654220.caution: The rules must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654225.summary: Add audit rules that record any write or attribute change to /etc/group, so group creation, membership changes, and removals are logged and can be tied to an account.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654225.caution: The rules must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654230.summary: Add audit rules that record any write or attribute change to /etc/gshadow, so changes to group passwords and administrators are logged and can be tied to an account.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654230.caution: The rules must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654235.summary: Add audit rules that record any write or attribute change to the old-passwords file /etc/security/opasswd, so tampering with password history is logged and can be tied to an account.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654235.caution: The check looks for /etc/security/opasswd while the fix text uses the path /etc/opasswd; use the path the check expects so the rule actually satisfies the assessment.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654240.summary: Add audit rules that record any write or attribute change to /etc/passwd, so account creation, modification, and removal are logged and can be tied to an account.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654240.caution: The rules must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654245.summary: Add audit rules that record any write or attribute change to /etc/shadow, so password changes and account lockouts or removals are logged and can be tied to an account.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654245.caution: The rules must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654250.summary: Add audit rules that record any write or attribute change by a regular user to /var/log/faillock, the failed-login tracking file, so attempts to clear or alter lockout records are logged.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654250.caution: The rules must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654255.summary: Add audit rules that record any write or attribute change by a regular user to /var/log/lastlog, the last-login record, so attempts to alter login history are logged.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654255.caution: The rules must be loaded into the kernel to take effect immediately.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654265.summary: Configure the audit system to shut the machine down (panic) if the audit subsystem hits a critical failure, so the system never keeps running without the ability to record what is happening.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654265.caution: A critical audit failure will halt the system outright, so only apply this where availability is not documented as an overriding concern and audit storage is well monitored.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654270.summary: Set the audit system so a user's login UID cannot be changed once it has been set at logon, ensuring every audited action stays tied to the person who originally logged in even after they switch accounts.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654270.caution: The audit daemon must be restarted for the change to take effect, and any software that legitimately resets the login UID will stop working.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654275.summary: Make the loaded audit rules immutable (the -e 2 setting as the last line) so no one, including root, can alter or disable auditing without rebooting the system.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-654275.caution: Once the rules are immutable any change to auditing requires a reboot, so finish all other audit rule changes first and make sure -e 2 is the final line.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-671015.summary: Every interactive user's stored password must be hashed with SHA-512 (a hash beginning with $6$); accounts whose passwords use a weaker hash must be locked until the password is reset with SHA-512.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-671015.caution: Locking accounts prevents those users from logging in until their passwords are regenerated, so coordinate the resets before locking anyone out.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-671025.summary: Make sure the pam_unix.so password line in /etc/pam.d/password-auth includes the sha512 option, so any new or changed password is stored using an approved hashing algorithm.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-671025.caution: Editing PAM files by hand can break logins if the syntax is wrong, and tools that regenerate PAM configuration may overwrite the change.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-211035.summary: Install rng-tools and keep the rngd service running so the hardware random number generator feeds entropy to the system, giving cryptographic operations a better source of randomness.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-211035.caution: Not applicable on systems running with kernel FIPS mode enabled; installing the package requires repository access.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212050.summary: Add pti=on to the kernel boot arguments for every installed kernel and to the GRUB defaults, so kernel page-table isolation is enabled and stays enabled across kernel updates, protecting against processor-based vulnerabilities such as Meltdown.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212050.caution: Page-table isolation carries a performance cost on some workloads and takes effect only after a reboot; a mistyped boot argument can prevent the system from booting.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212055.summary: Add audit=1 to the kernel boot arguments for every installed kernel and to the GRUB defaults, so processes that start before the audit daemon are still audited and the setting survives kernel updates.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-212055.caution: The change takes effect only after a reboot, and a mistyped boot argument can prevent the system from booting.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-214035.summary: Set clean_requirements_on_remove=True in the dnf configuration so that when a package is removed, dependencies that nothing else needs are removed too, keeping outdated and unused software off the system.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-214035.caution: Future package removals will also pull out orphaned dependencies, so review what dnf proposes to remove before confirming.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231020.summary: Put /var on its own file system rather than the root partition, so runaway growth of variable data such as logs or spools cannot fill the root file system and destabilize the machine.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231020.caution: Moving /var on an existing system requires downtime, enough free disk to hold the data, and a careful migration; getting it wrong can leave the system unbootable.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231025.summary: Put /var/log on its own file system so that heavy logging cannot fill the root or /var partition and so log storage can be sized and protected separately.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231025.caution: Migrating /var/log on a live system requires downtime and a correct data copy; services that hold log files open will need to be restarted.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231030.summary: Put the audit log directory (commonly /var/log/audit) on its own file system so that audit records cannot be crowded out by other logs and audit storage can be managed on its own.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231030.caution: Migrating audit data on an existing system requires downtime and careful copying; if the audit daemon is set to halt when storage is full, undersizing the new file system can bring the system down.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231195.summary: Prevent the cramfs compressed file system kernel module from ever loading by blacklisting it, since it is rarely needed and reduces the kernel's attack surface.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-231195.caution: If anything on the system genuinely uses cramfs, that use must be documented with the ISSO before applying this instead.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252025.summary: Set port 0 in the chrony configuration so the time daemon only acts as a client and does not answer time requests from other machines on the network.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252025.caution: Not applicable if the machine is intentionally serving time to others; applying it there would cut off every client that depends on it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252030.summary: Set cmdport 0 in the chrony configuration so the time daemon cannot be managed or queried over the network, only locally.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-252030.caution: Any remote monitoring tool that queries chrony over the network will stop getting answers.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-291025.summary: Configure the USBGuard daemon to send its audit events to the Linux audit system, so USB device connections and policy decisions are recorded alongside other security events.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-291025.caution: Not a finding on virtual machines with no USB peripherals; the daemon must be restarted for the change to apply.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-412040.summary: Set a hard limit of ten concurrent login sessions per account in the PAM limits configuration, so a compromised or misbehaving account cannot open unlimited sessions and exhaust system resources.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-412040.caution: Accounts or automation that legitimately need more than ten simultaneous sessions will be refused; any higher limit must be documented with the ISSO.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-651030.summary: Make sure the file integrity tool (AIDE by default) checks access control lists on every file and directory it monitors, so unauthorized changes to ACLs are detected during integrity scans.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-651030.caution: After changing the AIDE configuration the baseline database needs to be regenerated or the next scan will report widespread differences.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-651035.summary: Make sure the file integrity tool (AIDE by default) checks extended attributes on every file and directory it monitors, so unauthorized changes to attributes such as SELinux labels are detected during integrity scans.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-651035.caution: After changing the AIDE configuration the baseline database needs to be regenerated or the next scan will report widespread differences.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653120.summary: Set the kernel boot argument audit_backlog_limit to at least 8192 on every installed kernel so that audit events generated before the audit daemon starts are buffered rather than dropped.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653120.caution: The change takes effect only after a reboot, and any boot-argument edit should be double-checked to avoid an unbootable kernel entry.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653055.summary: Tell the audit daemon what to do when a log file hits its size limit, normally rotating to a new file, so auditing keeps running instead of silently stopping or filling the disk.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653055.caution: Rotation without enough max_log_file/num_logs headroom can discard older audit records; make sure logs are also being shipped off-box.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653060.summary: Configure the audit daemon to stamp each record with the hostname (or FQDN/numeric address) before logs are offloaded, so a central log server can tell which machine an event came from.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653060.caution: The audit daemon must be restarted for the change to take effect.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653065.summary: Set how the audit daemon reacts when its internal event queue overflows, for example sending to syslog, so audit events are not silently dropped under load.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653065.caution: Choosing halt will shut the system down on queue overflow; syslog or single are safer defaults unless mission rules require halting.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653070.summary: Point the audit daemon's failure notifications at an account (root, or a security-staff mailbox) so an administrator or the ISSO actually hears about audit processing failures.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653070.caution: Notification only works if local mail for that account is actually read or forwarded somewhere; restart auditd after the change.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653075.summary: Make sure the audit daemon records events generated on the local machine, not only events forwarded from elsewhere, so local activity is not left out of the audit trail.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653075.caution: Restart the audit daemon after editing the setting.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653080.summary: Ensure the audit log files are group-owned by root or the dedicated logging group named in auditd.conf, so ordinary users cannot read the audit trail through group permissions.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653080.caution: Use the group actually configured as log_group; picking a different group can break log readers that rely on it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653085.summary: Make root the owner of the audit log directory (by default /var/log/audit) so no other account can read, replace or remove the audit logs.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653090.summary: Restrict permissions on every audit log file so only the owner can read or write it (0600, or 0640 for the current log when a separate logging group is configured), preventing unauthorized reading of the audit trail.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653090.caution: Apply the 0640/0440 variant when log_group is set to a non-root group, otherwise tools in that group lose read access.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653095.summary: Have the audit daemon flush buffered records to disk at least every 100 records, so a crash or power loss does not lose a large batch of audit events.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653095.caution: Very low values increase disk writes on busy systems; restart auditd after the change.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653100.summary: Use the ENRICHED audit log format so user and group names, hostnames and similar details are resolved and written into each record, letting investigators identify who or what caused an event.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653100.caution: Enriched records are larger, so check log sizing; restart auditd after the change.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653105.summary: Confirm the audit daemon is actually writing its records to disk rather than only forwarding them, so there is a local audit trail to review.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653105.caution: Restart the audit daemon after editing the setting.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653110.summary: Lock down the audit configuration files (auditd.conf and everything under /etc/audit/rules.d) to owner-only permissions so only root can change which events get audited.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653125.summary: Create a Postfix mail alias that forwards root's mail to the ISSO or SA account, so audit failure messages sent to root reach a real person.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653125.caution: The alias only helps if the target account or mailbox is actually monitored; run newaliases after editing or the change is ignored.

claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653130.summary: Install the audispd-plugins package, which provides the plugins (such as remote logging) the audit daemon needs to forward audit records to a central server.
claude-cowork-2026-09:RHEL-09-653130.caution: Requires access to a package repository; installing the package alone does not configure remote logging.
